title: The ghazal form

segments.voice: The long night is tonight: candles, fruit, Ray's old library book, Theo pretending he isn't nervous. Zoe has written two couplets of her own to read. Ray reads them over her shoulder and says: put your name in the last one. She thinks he's teasing. He isn't. That's yesterday's question answered, and it's the rule of the ghazal.
screen: `THE LONG NIGHT IS TONIGHT.` → `PUT YOUR NAME IN THE LAST ONE.` → `THE RULE OF THE GHAZAL.`

segments.voice: A ghazal is built of couplets, and each couplet stands on its own, like a bead on a string. At the end of each couplet comes the radif, a refrain, the same word or phrase every time, with a rhyme just before it. That's the knock in Rumi's last ghazal: reha kon, mobtala kon. And in the last couplet, the poet signs his pen name, the takhallus, often speaking to himself. Hafiz does it at the end of his very first ghazal: Hafiz, if you want presence, don't be absent from Him; when you meet the one you long for, let the world go. That signature carries a real Sufi teaching. The word is hozur, presence: to be with God, not elsewhere in your head. The poet's own name becomes a reminder he can't dodge. So Zoe's two couplets get a refrain, and in the last line, her own name, telling herself the truth.
screen: `COUPLETS, EACH A BEAD.` · `RADIF: THE REFRAIN.` · `TAKHALLUS: THE NAME IN THE LAST LINE.` · `HOZUR: DON'T BE ABSENT.` · then, large: `MY COUPLETS.`

segments.voice: Write two couplets by hand, each ending on the same short refrain, a few words like still here or tonight. In the last line, put your own name, and say something true to yourself, the way Hafiz did.
The ghazal form: couplets that stand alone, a refrain at the end of each, and the poet's own name in the last.
Hold on to this: my couplets, signed in the last line. Hafiz, all eight days, done.

howItsDone: Persian, Urdu and Turkish poets write ghazals in couplets with a refrain (radif) and a rhyme, and sign the last couplet with a pen name (takhallus). Hafiz's ghazals are recited and sung in that shape.
